main_damage_causes: The film corpus provided is extremely limited — only two Knight Bus scenes from Prisoner of Azkaban are present, covering Ernie Prang (the bus driver), not Ernie Macmillan (the Hufflepuff student) who is the subject of the book corpus

Ernie Macmillan's rich book characterization — his arc from suspicious accuser in CoS to apologetic peer, his pompous but loyal DA membership, his prefect anxieties, his brave stand at the Battle of Hogwarts casting a Patronus — has no corresponding film corpus evidence to score against, meaning damage cannot be assessed from corpus alone

The absence of any Ernie Macmillan film scenes in the provided corpus prevents scoring of his most significant book moments: the CoS accusation and apology arc, his OotP DA participation and prefect hesitation, and his DH Battle of Hogwarts Patronus

damaging_scenes.scene: Film Corpus Scene 1-2 (Knight Bus scenes, PoA): Ernie Prang depicted as unnamed background driver
damaging_scenes.book_baseline: Book establishes Ernie Prang as a named character with small but distinct personality: he is an elderly wizard in thick glasses who grunts monosyllabic responses ('Ar'), shudders at mention of Azkaban guards ('them Azkaban guards give me the collywobbles'), and engages minimally but distinctly with Stan and Harry throughout the ride
damaging_scenes.film_portrayal: The film Knight Bus scenes contain no named 'Ernie Macmillan' — the film corpus shows Ernie Prang (the driver) is present but rendered as a purely functional, silent background figure described only as 'an unshaven wizard in thick glasses' with no dialogue, no name spoken, and no personality beats. All of the book's minor Ernie Prang characterization is absent. Note: Ernie Prang and Ernie Macmillan are different characters; the film corpus contains no appearance of Ernie Macmillan at all.
damaging_scenes.explanation: Ernie Prang's small personality (collywobbles line, monosyllabic presence) is lost in the film rendering him purely functional, but this is a minor background character moment with low adaptation stakes.
